newsitem.title: USA: NASD chief open to coordinate decimal trade shift.
newsitem.headline: NASD chief open to coordinate decimal trade shift.

text.p: The National Association of Securities Dealers's chairman, Frank Zarb, said Thursday he is open to coordinating a shift toward decimal stock quoting from fractions if the securities and investment community gives its stamp of approval to queries on such a move.

"We will have all that data within a month, and if it demonstratates that it's in the best interest to go forward with decimalization, then we will coordinate and attempt to work out a common timetable for implementation," Zarb told Reuters.

He warned, however, that a shift to decimal-based trades must be fully studied first. He raised concerns about the financial impact on smaller firms and whether or not the current regulatory scheme will work under that system.
"We are talking about the biggest financial system in the world. You don't go around throwing switches without being reasonably sure of what you are doing," he cautioned.
Zarb's comments came in the wake of the New York Stock Exchange's landmark board approval Thursday of a plan to drive quoting on the big board to decimals by the year 2000.

Supporters of the NYSE's latest move, which includes top lawmakers and Securities and Exchange Commission officials, say the shift could save investors billions of dollars annually because trading increments would be substantially lower than the current 12.5 minimum increment imposed since stocks can only be traded in eighths.

Rep. Michael Oxley, R-Ohio, who chairs the House Commerce subcommittee that oversees securities-related issues, said he expects the Nasdaq stock market will act in concert with other exchanges in narrowing stock trading increments.
"My sense is that (Zarb) feels he will have a very positive response from the majority of people he has polled and that it will propel them even further into this," Oxley told reporters.

Zarb said he hopes to report to Oxley's committee, other exchanges and others by the third week of July, after which NASD will help implement a timetable for moving to decimals if the report is favorable.
SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt has also called a meeting of exchange and clearing officials to help map out a system for shifting to decimals.
